inputs: The four RFC 4269 Appendix B vectors B.1-B.4, each with a 128-bit key and a 128-bit plaintext
expected: Every encryption matches the listed ciphertext and every decryption returns the original plaintext; the B.1 table also matches all sixteen round subkeys and per-round input states, the state after round i equals the input state of round i+1, and the state after round 16 equals the ciphertext halves
limitations: Four fixed vectors; they cover different keys and plaintexts but do not prove resistance to cryptanalysis.

inputs: The all-zero B.1 key and the RFC 4269 KC constants, compared with the sixteen Ki0/Ki1 pairs listed in Appendix B.1
expected: K1=7C8F8C7EC737A22C, K2=FF276CDBA7CA684A and K16=7189115098B255B0; all sixteen Ki match the RFC table; the decryption schedule is the reverse of the encryption schedule
limitations: Only the all-zero key has published per-round subkeys; the other three vectors validate the schedule indirectly through their ciphertexts.

inputs: RFC 4269 Appendix A S0, S1 and SS0-SS3, the mask definitions m0=FC, m1=F3, m2=CF, m3=3F, and deterministic G/F samples
expected: S0 and S1 each have 256 entries; all four SS-boxes are reproduced from S0/S1 and the masks for all 256 inputs; S0[0]=A9, S1[0]=38, S0[255]=9A, S1[255]=B7; G(00000000)=B829B829, G(01234567)=27E4246B and F(K1,08090A0B0C0D0E0F)=8080BE54C0EF8C18
limitations: Structural and reproducibility checks, not an assessment of S-box nonlinearity or cryptographic strength.

inputs: Three fixed keys (B.1 zero key, B.3 key and B.4 key) times eight deterministic plaintext patterns, including the B.1 and B.2 official plaintexts
expected: All 24 encrypt/decrypt round trips return the plaintext; the same plaintext under different keys gives different ciphertexts; the three keys produce three pairwise distinct schedules
limitations: Deterministic round-trip tests only; they do not test modes, protocols, key management, side channels or randomness.
